works.title_cn: 明月 ：傳承 / 香港瑰麗酒店 x 香港故宮文化博物館
works.statement_en:
unlike all mooncake packagings in market, this full moon story is imaginary and inspiring which created by ai with scientific datas.
it blends transitional and contemporary chinese art and culture.
designer has joined hands with local artist with the world’s first artificial intelligence ink painter a.i. gemini,
to create a dialogue across time and space and reimagine the harvest moon through ink painting and state-of- the-art technology.
the design approach certainly reflects the both rosewood and hong kong palaces museum’s spirit,
prompting and embracing creative culture with spectrum from traditional to contemporary.
works.statement_cn:
與所有在市場出現之中秋節月餅禮盒設計方向截然不同... 這個副想像力之㘣月故事是由 AI 跟科學數據而創造出來的。
設計糅合嶄新，並傳承中國文化的精神。平面設計師跟本地視覺藝術家及他的 a.i. gemini ，
以中國傳統的水墨畫概念，融入古人對中秋滿月的想像及嫦娥四號完成世界首次月球背面軟着陸的相關數據。
利用由創新的人工智能所輔助的設計及跨越時空的對話，重新詮釋現代水墨畫的傳承。
這個設計的方向，正正反映香港瑰麗酒店和香港故宮文化博物館雙方的精神，
推廣和擁抱創意文化在傳統、傳承和未來的探索。

heaven & hell /

works.category_cn: 活動視覺 / 書籍 / 海報 / 推廣
works.statement_en:
“heaven and hell” is the theme of the agi 2012 held during the hong kong design conference and exhibition.
heaven and hell are relative,
there is always bad in good, and good in bad.
it is heaven and it is hell.
a long time ago, hong kong was a “shopping paradise” and then it also became a “gourmet paradise”.
heaven is perfection, is a dream,
a pursuit, an epitome...
a common line in movies – “there is a road to heaven but you shun it, there is no door to hell yet you break in…”
or, another oft-heard line,
“if i do not risk going to hell, no one will.”
heaven and hell exist in the mythical world.
heaven and hell exist in the religious world.
there is heaven and hell in the west.
there is heaven and hell in the east.
if hell is in the abyss between the east and the west,
then,
heaven should be up high,
closer to the sky…
in the buddhist world,
there are also two states of existence:
purified land (heaven) exists among us,
right before us, in our minds,
and so does hell.
one thought can take us to heaven,
another thought can bring us hell.
works.statement_cn:
《天堂與地獄》是AGI 二○一二在香港舉辦設計會議及活動的主題。
天堂與地獄是一個相對的，好中有壞，壞中有好的概念。
也是地獄。也是天堂。
很久很久以前，
香港被譽為「購物天堂」
後又被稱「美食天堂」。
天堂是美好至極，是夢，是追求，
是指標…
電影常出現這句話：「天堂有路你不走，地獄無門你闖進來…」
另外一句：「我不入地獄，誰入地獄。」
神話世界有天堂地獄。
宗教世界有天堂地獄。
西方有天堂地獄。
東方有天堂地獄。
如果地獄是在東西方之間地底最深處，
那麼，
天堂是較近哪一方之天空上面…
佛的世界也有另兩角度：
淨土（天堂）就在人間，
地獄也在眼前。
一念天堂，一念地獄。

改變我往後創作和做人的思路和價值觀。

這可能是我工作以來，最有效的宣傳案子。

works.title_en:
seeing words in hong kong / redwhiteblue //
words talking / self talking
works.title_cn:
香港看字 / 紅白藍 //
字言。字語
works.statement_en:
it is said that “a picture tells more than a thousand words”.
if a picture can speak more than a thousand words, then,
what can be offered by a picture with just “a few words”?
words are used to tell different stories by respective interpretation,
being fermented and polished along with time, the plot becomes more vivid and touching.
words can be compelling, but sometimes be taken apart.
ideas can be put into words, but sometimes you have to read between the lines.
at the crossroad, reminding me of the lyrics of “midnight whisper”
by cantopop singer sam hui: babbling nonsense, more typos. however, we both know what's in our hearts.
knowing but not knowing, conversing with myself ruthlessly.
(a tribute to the heroes and unsung heroes written in the city of hong kong in the past forty years,
granting me unlimited imagination and inspiration).
works.statement_cn:
人家説 a picture tells more than a thousand words 。
如果一幅照片能説多過千言萬語，
那麼，一張有「三言兩語」的照片，可能給我們什麼...
文字落在不同人的手中，訴説不同的故事心聲，
與時間磨合發酵，情節愈發立體、動人。
有時字字鏗鏘，有時説文會被解字。
有時白紙黑字，有時唯有字裡行間。
十字街頭，想起 sam hui 一句歌詞：
糊言亂語更多錯字，總之兩心知。
在知還不知當中，好好地、狠狠地，自言自語。
（ 向四十年來親身看見在香港我城書寫其中的英雄和無名英雄致意，
賦與我無限想像和靈感。）
seeing words in hong kong / redwhiteblue //

cells.text_en:
in hong kong walk on, tai ping’s most demanding level of craftsmanship in recent decades,
anothermountainman reinterprets his iconic red white blue series by creating a sophisticated,
photorealistic design that gives the illusion of a rippled textile.
to showcase the intricate texture of the original fabric, tai ping furthered its exploration into artistic production with a mural-standard execution,
an approach that is beyond the reach of technological assistance due to the intricacy of the design.
abandoning computer-generated templates, artisans performed their work directly on the canvas,
relying on their unparalleled skills and artistic interpretation in order to bring the image to life – based solely on a photo reference.
to guide the artisans, the first layer of the template was hand-painted onto a 3 x 6m canvas,
which divided the carpet into 71,200 small grids of 1.59 x 1.59cm, followed by a second layer of the sketched design.
each grid was carefully analysed to ensure every millimetre of the carpet was accurately defined.
the artisans then applied a combination of yarns to the canvas using a hand-tufting gun to fill each grid,
crafting in horizontal, vertical or diagonal directions.
smooth gradation, dynamic curves and clean lines, together with the regular collocation of red/white grids or blue/white grids throughout,
mark the challenges from which this artisanal piece grows.
the complex design required the workshop to appoint four seasoned artisans with over 25 years of hand-tufting experience,
as well as 10 craftsmen from various departments including colour matching, sketching, stencilling & brushing,
colour separation, and colour marking & processing.
the carpet was made using 64 different hues of red, white and blue along with 628 colour combinations in grade a new zealand wool and silk yarns.
from inception to completion, this extraordinary textile took 12 months to complete.
cells.text_cn:
將又一山人的「紅白藍」布料皺摺形態藝術照片以寫實主義呈現於地氈香港前行，
生產及手工複雜程度為近年所未見。
為展現原裝布料複雜的質感及達至對圖案輪廓的嚴格要求，
需要採用壁畫形式設計及製作，
意指設計、生產及手工複雜程度超越電腦程式所及，
需要工藝師及工匠單憑經驗及參照藝術照片，在沒有任何電腦程式協助直接上畫及織造。
工藝師先在三米 × 六米的畫布上起第一層畫稿，
將其分劃成七萬一千二百個 1.59×1.59 釐米的小格子；
然後將設計圖案勾畫出來，此為第二層畫稿。
其後在每個小格子內進行技術分析，以確保每一部份都極其精細準確。
工匠以人手簇絨槍在每個小格子用四組不同的混合紗線及按水平、垂直及對角方向來織造。
既要達致自然過渡效果，也要保持線條的暢順和整體均一，
還要呈現出紅白格或藍白格的規律配搭，對工匠的技藝水平挑戰極高。
太平共起用了四位具二十五年以上經驗的資深手工簇絨工匠及
十位不同崗位的工藝師包括配色，放畫，刷畫，分色，標色及加工來織造此地氈；
使用甲級紐西蘭羊毛及真絲，
共六十四種不同深淺的紅、白和藍色紗線及六百二十八組混合紗線織造而成。
整個項目由策劃、設計至完工需時整整十二個月的時間。

works.statement_en:
the rise of causes is simply because of one’s subjectivity and wishful thinking.
more than ten years ago, i had a conversation with my friends about the forms of funeral
and how to see people for the last time.
i expressed my concerns: the melancholy, the hazy and smoky environment and
the colors in traditional chinese-style funeral were things i found uncomfortable…
we opened the end of the conversations.
the most concerns of all, in my thinking, was about coffin.
1. it was environmental unfriendly. even the state-of-the-art eco-coffin was after all one kind of
commodities which came into being thanks to “death”, it was a luxury item for its one-time usage.
2. its over-design and the curvy outlook annoyed me for i am a perfectionist
in pursuing straight lines and the orderly square shape.
(that was before a relatively more minimal design of paper coffin was brought out in the market.)
3. most of all, the alienation. i asked myself for what reasons people have to be wrapped,
in their very last moment,in an object or space that makes no connection to their lives and carries no emotions?
as i thought about all these, i decided to make a sofa bed for my own use
for up to 30 or 50 years until i passed away in it.
how environmental friendly it is, and how intimate it is to me…
as i thought more deeply, i knew that by interacting intimately with the sofa bed everyday
i could experience how “death” is regarded as part of one’s life.
it would be a task and learning for me to come face-to-face with my own life.
impermanent. between a sofa bed and a coffin.
impermanent. between this life, death and the next life.
in between. there should be the will to cherish… it should be positive… proactive… and free…
impermanent. the experiencing the life.
works.statement_cn:
緣起，只因主觀願望，只因一廂情願 ⋯
十多年前與朋友説起葬禮的形式，如何與他人見最後一面。
表白了我關心的是：怕悲情、怕香燭煙火、怕傳統中式葬禮的多顏色⋯⋯
開了話題，拜託了朋友，往後再看吧。
再想下去，最不安的要算是棺木這環節吧。
接受不了它不夠環保，就算是近年面世的環保棺材，
也是因死而「生」的市場產品；
只可使用一次的奢侈產品。
接受不了它不夠簡約和多弧線外型的設計﹝當時還未出現紙棺材這比較簡約的造型﹞，
正因為一向自知是個對直線、四正追求「完美」主義者。
最最接受不了的是陌生感受。心裡問：為何在離世的最後一刻、伴著的空間，
竟是被那個與一生無關、沒時日感情、沒感覺的東西包圍著。
想了想了，決定做張梳化牀，用它三、五十年，然後裹身一同離去。
符合環保原則，多麼親切，多好 ⋯⋯
再想，藉著每天親近梳化牀的互動，親身感受「死」是人生的一部份這概念；
親近面對自己人生的一個功課。
無常。是梳化牀和棺木之間。
無常。是今生和死亡和來生之間。
之間。應該是珍惜⋯是正面⋯是積極⋯是自在⋯
無常。是體驗人生。

works.statement_en:
ZONE 1 /
brief time line introduction of
chinese design and craft in history
(video and craftworks).
ZONE 2 /
the literature of craft and production for
empires’s families (from different historical periods).
ZONE 3 /
6 crafted treasury object series from different materials /
jade / wood craving / glass / enamel /…
educational details on different materials with samples and tools.
4 vertical testimonial videos from hong kong artisans,
express their passion on materials,
and the way they see the industries going forward for next generation.
ZONE 4 /
chinese design and craft treasures.
a circular radiation display includes objects of
clothing / dinning / living / stationary for empires’s families.
ZONE 5 /
chinese design spirit /
a long video wall of 4 interviews from hong kong master designers,
to tell their passion and values in design and creativity
within chinese roots and lead to now and future.
artistic director stanley wong (anothermountainman) in the last video,
to conclude the whole show,
the importance and meaning to persuade design and craft
in our own culture from history, and pass on 傳承 to our future,
also elaborate the artistic statement
which from the very beginning of the exhibition.
result /
huge positive responses from all stakeholders including
hong kong public / hong hong kong youngsters / overseas visitors /
hong kong cultural groups / hong kong and beijing palace museum boards /
as ex board chairman bernard chan said,
‘it a unique hong kong story rides on chinese cultural history,
demonstrated a pride of hong kong…’
works.statement_cn:
第一區 /
中國設計與工藝的歷史簡介
（影片及工藝品）。
第二區 /
歷代皇室的工藝與製作文獻。
第三區 /
六個以不同物料製作的珍品系列 /
玉 / 木雕 / 玻璃 / 琺瑯 /……
以樣本及工具講解各種物料的知識。
四段直幅訪談影片，由香港工匠
細說他們對物料的熱情，
以及他們眼中行業如何走向下一代。
第四區 /
中國設計與工藝珍品。
環形放射式陳列，包括歷代皇室的
衣 / 食 / 住 / 文房用品。
第五區 /
中國設計精神 /
一道長影像牆，播放四位香港設計大師的訪談，
細說他們在中國文化根源上的設計與創作熱情和價值，
並延伸至當下與未來。
藝術總監黃炳培（又一山人）於最後一段影片
為整個展覽作結：
在自身文化與歷史中追求設計與工藝的重要與意義，
並將之傳承至未來；
同時闡述展覽開首的藝術宣言。
成果 /
各方持份者反應熱烈正面，包括
香港市民 / 香港年輕人 / 海外訪客 /
香港文化團體 / 香港故宮文化博物館及北京故宮博物院董事局；
正如前董事局主席陳智思所言：
「這是一個獨特的香港故事，以中國文化歷史為根基，
展現了香港的驕傲……」

works.statement_en:
life is beautiful, savouring the meaning of life.
in our fast-paced society, we sweat everyday between “living a life” and “survival”
hardly finding the time and mood to savour the meaning of life. there are truly many
small things in life that are worthy of savouring.
the ifc mall is an iconic shopping mall in hong kong. it has a human and personal
touch, bringing together the fine things of our lives, which are also a part of our lives.
let’s start from here with our interpretation of “life is beautiful”.
let us explore the meaning of life together.
works.statement_cn:
《生命是美麗的》細味生活的意義。
今天在步伐急速的社會中，大家每日於「生活」與「生存」之間疲於奔命，
鮮有心思時間細味生活的意義，感受人生。
事實上，生活當中種種的細節，都值得大家細心欣賞。
ifc商場是本港具代表性的商場之一，具有親和力及人性化的一面，
匯聚大家的生活點滴，亦是大家生活的一部分。
正好以此出發，演繹「生命是美麗的」，與大眾正面探討生命。

works.statement_en:
positive hongkong, redwhiteblue
redwhiteblue is existence, participation,
dedication and giving.
redwhiteblue is perseverance, diligence and endurance
redwhiteblue represents each and every hong kong people of the 1960s and 1970s
after the handover, 50 years unchanged....
positive, motivated
anothermountainman
redwhiteblue  body  heart  soul
tough and dependable, but flexible and adaptable.
the redwhiteblue series not only symbolise the perseverance,
flexibility and diligence of the hong kong people,
it also represents the hard work
that the rehabilitated patients of mental illness
gave in making these fabric products,
it is an important first step in achieving self-recovery
and rebuilding the health of the “body  heart  soul”
new life association
works.statement_cn:
正面香港 紅白藍
紅白藍是存在、參與、耕耘和付出
紅白藍是堅持、拼博、和捱苦
紅白藍是代表我們香港六、七十年代的	每一份子
這是我們香港回歸後
應一直保持五十年不變的…
正面積極
又一山人
紅白藍 身 心 靈
堅韌可靠，卻又靈活多變的
紅白藍系列不僅象徵着香港人堅毅不屈、
靈活變通的拼博精神，它亦代表着
精神病康復者為製作出
精心布藝產品而付出的不懈努力，
為自我復元、重建健康之「身 心 靈」
踏出重要的一步
新生會

works.statement_en:
to have a bowl of rice, life is nurtured.
to take a bowl of tea, body and soul are enlivened.
to inside from outside.
from inside to outside.
back and forth.
give and take.
those inside a bowl,
can be consumed,
can nurture a life.
a family of three is a family.
three generations under the same roof also form a family.
heaven and earth, with all beings, are ultimately the same family.
together we form a true family.
concept & photography by anothermountainman
green bowl-scape by yu tek-li

works.statement_en:
fangsuo is not just a bookstore. nor is it an area.
it is an attitude, an advocate.
it is an attempt to boldly amplify aesthetics in everyday life.
in the vast, boundless space of the universe,
we encounter the wisdom and knowledge of old and new,
we meet with designers from far and wide,
we connect with our own hearts and minds.
fangsuo is a peaceful and quiet spot in the universe,
it’s now.
let us all gather here.
fangsuo, a community that began in china,
is a platform for culture and aesthetics to meet,
a space where sensuality and intellect reside,
a conjugation of knowledge, aesthetics and living.
in this wide expanse for nurturing and practice,
people pursue truth, feel beauty,
experience the power that peace and tranquillity bring.
